sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandatory biodiesel B40 and solar rooftop targets are creating captive demand for domestic renewable producers, insulating them from global price volatility.
The nickel downstreaming policy, coupled with battery storage mandates, is structurally boosting climate-tech players like VKTR and BRPT beyond just power generation.
US climate-tech names are increasingly exposed to IRA subsidy uncertainty and high interest rates, making them less attractive relative to Indonesia's state-backed energy transition.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesian renewables leaders TOBA, VKTR, and BRPT, as the +3.34% ID surge signals sustained policy tailwinds and foreign inflows. Rotate out of US laggards like SEDG, which face margin pressure despite the bounce. Prioritize names with domestic offtake contracts and nickel-linked storage exposure for Q3.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's domestic consumption is structurally accelerating on rising middle-class spending and government stimulus, decoupling from US consumer weakness.
Local FMCG and consumer discretionary brands are gaining share against multinationals, driven by aggressive distribution expansion and digital-native marketing.
Rupiah stability and easing inflation are boosting real purchasing power, creating a durable tailwind for consumer equities despite global volatility.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into the sharp ID consumer rally: BIKE, CBUT, POLU, and PADA show momentum on domestic demand recovery and rupiah stability, but avoid chasing the full basket—take profits on ZONE and AGAR as they are overextended. Favor names with strong earnings visibility and local-brand penetration; expect continued outperformance vs US peers as Indonesia's consumption cycle accelerates into year-end.

Rotate into high-beta names like PPGL and HUMI for outsized upside, but lock in TRUK and CHRW as defensive core. Expect continued momentum over 4-6 weeks on rate-cut tailwinds and e-commerce restocking.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's crypto tax reform and exchange licensing (Bappebti) is funneling domestic retail liquidity into global altcoins, amplifying beta moves like VET and SPX beyond their offshore fundamentals.
Solana's fee-revenue growth and institutional staking products make it the structural winner for Indonesian funds seeking yield without custody complexity.
Chainlink's cross-chain interoperability standard is the durable pick as Indonesian banks pilot tokenized RWA settlements, tying LINK demand to local fintech adoption.
sectors.ai: Buy the VET-led alt surge as a beta trade into Indonesia's retail crypto reopening, but rotate profits into SOL and LINK for sustained institutional flow. VET's +21% is a one-off China narrative spike; take partial gains. Add SOL on dips below $150 and LINK on any sub-$18 pullback—both have real DeFi and oracle demand. Trim ENA and TAO into strength; their rallies lack volume confirmation.
